questions.question: A loss of 12% gets converted into a profit of 8.5% when the selling price of an article is increased by ₹164. The cost price of article is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Loss = 12%

Profit = 8.5%

Difference in profit % and loss % = 164

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Cost price + (Cost price × profit%)

Selling price = Cost price - (Cost price × loss%)

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100x

Selling price of 1st case = 100x - 100x × 12%

⇒100x - (100 × 12/100) = 88x

Selling price of 2nd case = 100x + 100x × 8.5%

⇒ 100x + (100x × 8.5/100) = 108.5x

According to the question,

108.5x - 88x = 164

⇒ 20.5x = 164

⇒ x = (164/20.5)

⇒ x = 8

So, the cost price of the article = 100 × 8 = Rs. 800

**∴ The cost price of the article is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let CP = 100 units

According to the question

108% of CP - 88% of CP = 164

⇒ 108.5 units - 88 units = Rs. 164

⇒ 20.5 units = Rs. 164

⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 8

∴ CP = 100 × 8 = Rs.800

Hence, The cost price of the article is ₹800.

questions.question: On the sum of the money, the simple interest (rate of interest r) for 3 year is the same as compound interest (rate of interest R) for 2 year. What is the relation between the rates of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate 3 years **Simple Interest** and 2 years **Compound Interest**: 3r/100 = (R/100)² + 2R/100.

Multiply by 10000 to remove denominators: 300r = R² + 200R.

Complete the square by adding 100² (10000) to both sides: R² + 200R + 10000 = 10000 + 300r.

(R + 100)² = 10000 + 300r.

Taking square root: R + 100 = √(10000 + 300r).

**∴ The correct answer is R + 100 = √10000+300r.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal** = P, **SI rate** = r, **SI time** = 3 years, **CI rate** = R, **CI time** = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × r × t) / 100; CI = P[(1 + R / 100)t − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdcc80981ea4a14df0e5dd583fbc1aab99cafcc0307439c15e84b2f7eabb4ae8.png] 

⇒ SI = (P × r × 3) / 100 = 3Pr / 100

⇒ CI = P[(1 + R / 100)² − 1] = P[1 + (R / 100)² + 2(R / 100) − 1]

⇒ CI = P[(R² / 10000) + (2R / 100)]

⇒ 3Pr / 100 = P[(R² / 10000) + (2R / 100)]

⇒ 3r / 100 = (R² + 200R) / 10000

⇒ 300r = R² + 200R

⇒ R² + 200R − 300r = 0

⇒ Applying quadratic formula: R = [−200 ± √(200² − 4 × 1 × (−300r))] / 2

⇒ R = [−200 + √(40000 + 1200r)] / 2

⇒ R = [−200 + 2 × √(10000 + 300r)] / 2

⇒ R = −100 + √(10000 + 300r)

⇒ R + 100 = √(10000 + 300r)

**∴ The correct answer is R + 100 = √10000+300r.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference (D) is P(R/100)². For 3 years, D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

Effective CI rate for 2 years is x + y + (xy/100). If rate is R, effective rate = 2R + R²/100.

Amount in CI

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where n is the number of compounding periods.</p

questions.question: Find the third proportional of (b² - a²) and (b² - ab).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two terms **A** and **B**, the **third proportional** (C) is calculated as **C = B² / A**.

Identify terms: **A = (b² − a²) = (b − a)(b + a)** and **B = (b² − ab) = b(b − a)**.

Apply trick: **C = [b(b − a)]² / [(b − a)(b + a)]**.

Simplify: **C = [b²(b − a)²] / [(b − a)(b + a)] = (b²(b − a)) / (b + a)**.

**∴ The correct answer is (b²(b−a))/(b+a).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (A) = **(b² − a²)**

Second term (B) = **(b² − ab)**

**Formula Used:**

If **x** is the **third proportional** of **A** and **B**, then **A : B :: B : x**, which implies **x = B² / A**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7568d86c49c40576d94fcbb9180deff0888abe76324341fe52b0fc9bd9123929.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **third proportional** be **x**.

⇒ **x = (b² − ab)² / (b² − a²)**

⇒ **x = [b(b − a)]² / [(b − a)(b + a)]**

⇒ **x = [b² × (b − a) × (b − a)] / [(b − a) × (b + a)]**

⇒ Cancel the common term **(b − a)** from numerator and denominator.

⇒ **x = (b²(b − a)) / (b + a)**

**∴ The correct answer is (b²(b−a))/(b+a).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is given by **√(ab)**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the **fourth proportional** **d** is calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.

Continued Proportion

Numbers **a**, **b**, **c** are in **continued proportion** if **a/b = b/c**, which implies **b² = ac**.</p

questions.question: The total population of a town is 5500. The number of males and females increases by 5% and 10% respectively and resulting population becomes 6000. Find the number of men in the town.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **increase** in population = 6000 − 5500 = 500.

Assume all 5500 were **males**: Increase = 5% of 5500 = 275.

Assume all 5500 were **females**: Increase = 10% of 5500 = 550.

By **Alligation** on increase values: (550 − 500) : (500 − 275) = 50 : 225 = 2 : 9.

Number of **men** = (2 / 11) × 5500 = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **total population** = 5500, **Final population** = 6000, **Male increase** = 5%, **Female increase** = 10%.

**Formula Used:** Total Increase = (Increase% of Males) + (Increase% of Females)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e3c72731cee7293f9d66f1fbb1cb61373dfb12c8feaa03375697b1db088a32.png] 

Let the number of **males** be x and **females** be (5500 − x).

⇒ 5% of x + 10% of (5500 − x) = 500

⇒ 0.05x + 0.10(5500 − x) = 500

⇒ 0.05x + 550 − 0.10x = 500

⇒ −0.05x = 500 − 550

⇒ −0.05x = −50

⇒ x = 50 / 0.05

⇒ x = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Original Value) / Original Value] × 100.

Alligation Method in Population

Ratio of two groups = (Higher % change − Average % change) : (Average % change − Lower % change).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.</p

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is three times its height. The width of the cuboid is half of the sum of its height and length, if five times the width is equal to 100 cm, then what is the total surface area of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given 5 × **Width** = 100 ⇒ **Width (w)** = 20 cm.

Relationship: **Width** = (**Length** + **Height**) ÷ 2. Since **Length** = 3 × **Height**, then 20 = (3h + h) ÷ 2 ⇒ 20 = 2h.

Thus, **Height (h)** = 10 cm and **Length (l)** = 30 cm.

**Total Surface Area** = 2(lw + wh + hl) = 2(600 + 200 + 300) = 2200 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 2200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length (l)** = 3h

**Width (w)** = (h + l) ÷ 2

5 × w = 100 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f65b9a9efa5be56b2ed0df93fb9601159f37deda6b2634d60b248e2c1f63580.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2(lw + wh + hl)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5w = 100 ⇒ w = 20 cm

⇒ w = (h + 3h) ÷ 2 ⇒ 20 = 4h ÷ 2

⇒ 20 = 2h ⇒ **Height (h)** = 10 cm

⇒ **Length (l)** = 3 × 10 = 30 cm

⇒ **TSA** = 2[(30 × 20) + (20 × 10) + (10 × 30)]

⇒ **TSA** = 2[600 + 200 + 300]

⇒ **TSA** = 2[1100] = 2200 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 2200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Volume = Length × Width × Height (l × w × h).

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical faces (excluding top and bottom) is given by LSA = 2 × h × (l + w).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is √(l² + w² + h²).</p

questions.question: The primary agent that helps in the decomposition of biodegradable matter in domestic sewage is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacterium**__.

__
 
• **Bacteria** play a crucial role in the decomposition of biodegradable matter in domestic sewage.
 
• They break down organic compounds into simpler substances, which can be further processed and removed from the sewage.
 
• Different types of bacteria are involved in various stages of sewage treatment, including **aerobic** and **anaerobic bacteria**.
 
• **Aerobic bacteria** require oxygen to break down organic matter, while **anaerobic bacteria** do not.
 
• Effective sewage treatment relies on maintaining the right balance and environment for these bacteria to thrive.
 
• This biological process helps in reducing the **BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand)** of the sewage, making it safer to release into the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• Chloride is primarily used in water treatment for disinfection and killing harmful pathogens.
 
• It does not play a role in the decomposition of organic matter in sewage.
 
 
 
• **Nitrate**__
 __
 
• Nitrate is a compound that can be formed during the decomposition process, but it is not an agent of decomposition itself.
 
• High levels of nitrates in water can lead to environmental issues such as eutrophication.
 
 
 
• **Phosphate**__
 
 
• Phosphate is another compound that can be found in sewage, often from detergents and fertilizers.
 
• Like nitrate, it is not involved in the decomposition process but can contribute to water pollution if not properly managed.

questions.question: ABCD is a parallelogram in which ∠ ACB = 40°, ∠ BAC = 80°, then ∠ ADC is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram** ABCD, diagonal AC divides it into two congruent triangles ΔABC and ΔADC.

Sum of angles in **ΔABC** = 180°.

∠ABC = 180° − (∠BAC + ∠ACB) = 180° − (80° + 40°) = 60°.

In a parallelogram, **opposite angles** are equal, so ∠ADC = ∠ABC.

∠ADC = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallelogram **ABCD** where ∠ACB = 40° and ∠BAC = 80°.

**Formula Used:**

1. Angle Sum Property of a triangle: The sum of interior angles is 180°.

2. Properties of a **parallelogram**: Opposite angles are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcf215057dd12123b8cf0b3a80022bc12914c0c1b867762b83d46e79cef6e9d3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In triangle **ABC**, the three angles are ∠ABC, ∠BAC, and ∠ACB.

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠BAC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC + 80° + 40° = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC + 120° = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC = 180° − 120°

⇒ ∠ABC = 60°

⇒ In **parallelogram ABCD**, the opposite angles are equal (∠ADC = ∠ABC).

⇒ ∠ADC = 60°

questions.question: Which is the most important international agreement for conserving all biodiversity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convention on Biological Diversity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most important international agreement for conserving all biodiversity is the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). **
 
• The CBD is an international treaty that was adopted in **1992 **with the aim of conserving biodiversity, promoting the sustainable use of its components, and ensuring the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of the utilization of genetic resources.
 
• The CBD is the** only international treaty that specifically focuses on all three aspects of biodiversity conservation: genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convention on Ballast Water (CBW)** is an international treaty that aims to prevent the spread of harmful aquatic organisms through ballast water.

 
 
• Ballast water is water that is taken on board ships to stabilize them, and it can contain a variety of organisms, including plankton, fish larvae, and microorganisms.
 
• Some of these organisms can be invasive and can **cause significant harm to marine ecosystems. **
 
• The CBW sets standards for the treatment and discharge of ballast water to reduce the risk of introducing harmful organisms.
 
 
 
• **UNCLOS** is the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
 
 
• It is a comprehensive agreement that covers all aspects of the use and management of the oceans and marine resources.
 
• UNCLOS includes provisions that are relevant to biodiversity conservation, such as the obligation to protect the marine environment and the requirement to conduct environmental impact assessments for activities that may have a significant impact on the marine environment.
 
 
 
• **CITES **is the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora.
 
 
• It is an international agreement that aims to regulate the international trade in endangered species of wild animals and plants.
 
• CITES does not deal with all aspects of biodiversity conservation, but it is an important tool for protecting endangered species from overexploitation.

**Given:**

Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at a point F outside the circle.

AF = 12 cm

BF = 4 cm

CF = 16 cm

**Concept used:**

If two chords AB and CD of a circle are cut at a point F outside the circle then,

AF × BF = CF × DF

So, according to the concept,

AF × BF = CF × DF

⇒ 12 × 4 = 16 × a

⇒ 48 = 16a

⇒ a = 48/16

CD = CF - DF

⇒ CD = 16 - 3

⇒ CD = 13 cm

**∴ The length of CD is 13 cm.**

questions.question: Which of the following fuel responsible for fire categorized as a Class D fuel?

options.text: Carbon-based products such as wood and paper.
Combustible materials where electricity may be present.
Combustible metals such as aluminum, magnesium, titanium and zirconium.

questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Class D Fires**

 
• Class D fires involve combustible metals. These types of fires are particularly dangerous and challenging to extinguish due to the chemical properties and high burning temperatures of the metals involved. Common metals that fall under this category include aluminum, magnesium, titanium, and zirconium.

**Characteristics of Combustible Metals:**

 
• **High Burning Temperatures:** Combustible metals burn at extremely high temperatures, which can exceed 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit. This makes them difficult to extinguish with water or standard fire extinguishers.
 
• **Reactivity with Water:** Many combustible metals react violently with water, producing flammable hydrogen gas and potentially causing explosions. Therefore, using water to extinguish a Class D fire can exacerbate the situation.
 
• **Specialized Extinguishing Agents:** Class D fires require specific extinguishing agents, such as dry powders designed to absorb heat and smother the fire. These agents are formulated to prevent the metal from reacting with oxygen and spreading the fire.

**Common Combustible Metals:**

 
• **Aluminum:** Commonly used in manufacturing and construction, aluminum can ignite when subjected to high temperatures or friction. Once ignited, it burns intensely and can be difficult to control.
 
• **Magnesium:** Found in automotive parts, aircraft, and some consumer products, magnesium burns with a bright white flame and reacts violently with water.
 
• **Titanium:** Used in aerospace and medical applications, titanium burns at high temperatures and is challenging to extinguish using conventional methods.
 
• **Zirconium:** Found in some industrial processes and specialized equipment, zirconium is highly flammable and requires careful handling to prevent fires.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower at a point on level ground is 45°. When moved 20 m towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. What is the height of the tower?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the angle of elevation changes from θ₁ to θ₂ while moving a distance **d** towards a tower of height **h**, the formula is:

**h = d ÷ (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)**

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (cot 45° − cot 60°)

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (1 − 1/√3) = 20√3 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ h = [20√3(√3 + 1)] ÷ 2 = 10(3 + √3) m

**∴ The correct answer is 10(3 + √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial angle θ₁ = 45°, Final angle θ₂ = 60°, Distance moved = 20 m.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc3e1660cffbea25428acb1ed5b15591d6f8743bcab1402dcb3c35586419273c.png] 

Let **h** be the **height of the tower** (CD) and **x** be the distance BC.

⇒ In ΔBCD: tan 60° = CD/BC ⇒ √3 = h/x ⇒ x = h/√3

⇒ In ΔACD: tan 45° = CD/AC ⇒ 1 = h/(20 + x)

⇒ 20 + x = h

⇒ 20 + h/√3 = h

⇒ h − h/√3 = 20

⇒ h(√3 − 1)/√3 = 20

⇒ h = 20√3 / (√3 − 1)

**Rationalizing** the denominator:

⇒ h = [20√3 × (√3 + 1)] / [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = [20(3 + √3)] / (3 − 1)

⇒ h = 20(3 + √3) / 2

⇒ h = 10(3 + √3) m

**∴ The correct answer is 10(3 + √3) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, and tan 30° = 1/√3. These are fundamental for **Heights and Distances** problems.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The **angle of elevation** is measured from the horizontal looking up, while the **angle of depression** is measured looking down. They are equal due to alternate interior angles.

questions.question: The average of 39% of A and 42% of B is equal to three-fifths of the difference of A and B. Find B as a percentage of A.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 39% of A and 42% of B is equal to three-fifths of the difference of A and B.

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

[A × (39/100) + B × (42/100)]/2 = (A - B) × (3/5)

⇒ [(39A + 42B)/100]/2 = (3A - 3B)/5

⇒ (39A + 42B)/200 = (3A - 3B)/5

⇒ (39A + 42B)/40 = (3A - 3B)

⇒ 39A + 42B = 120A - 120B

⇒ 42B + 120B = 120A - 39A

⇒ 162B = 81A

⇒ B/A = 81/162

So, ratio of B and A = 81 : 162 or 1 : 2

So, B = (1/2) × 100 of A or 50% of A

∴** Required answer is 50%.**

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a constable from 200 m. When the constable starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the constable is 8 km/h and thief runs at the speed of 6 km/h, then how far (in m) will the thief be able to run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between constable and thief = 200 m

Speed of constable = 8 km/h

Speed of thief = 6 km/h

**Formula used:**

Distance = relative speed × time

**Calculation:**

Distance = relative speed × time

⇒ 200 = (8 - 6) × (5/18) × time

⇒ 200 = 2 × (5/18) × time

⇒ Time = (200 × 18)/10

⇒ Time = 360 sec

Distance covered by thief = 6 × (5/18) × 360

⇒ 6 × 100 = 600 m

**∴ The correct answer is 600 m.**

__
 
• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are primarily used as **refrigerants** in air conditioning systems, refrigerators, and freezers.
 
• They are known for their ability to efficiently transfer heat, making them ideal for cooling applications.
 
• CFCs were once widely utilized due to their **low toxicity, stability, and non-flammability** properties.
 
• The most common CFC compounds used in refrigeration include **CFC-11, CFC-12, and CFC-113**.
 
• The use of CFCs in refrigerants has been significantly reduced globally due to their role in **ozone layer depletion**, as highlighted by the Montreal Protocol.

• CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere when exposed to UV radiation.

questions.question: What is the simple and easy method of artificial respiration?
questions.solution:
**Principle of Artificial Respiration:**

 
• Breathing in: By breathing the rescuer's breath into the lungs of the injured person, this person is supplied with the required oxygen.
 
• Breathing out: The injured person breathes out spontaneously due to the natural flexibility of the chest.
 
• The breath of the rescuer which is breathed into the injured person contains still 16 to 17 percentage by volume of oxygen.
 
• For sufficient respiration, 15 to 20 moderate breaths per minute given by the rescuer are required.
 
• Artificial respiration has to be continued until the injured person starts breathing or a medical doctor orders to stop the measure.

 

**Mouth-to-nose respiration:**

 
• Kneel down by the side of the injured person.
 
• Bend the head of the person back.
 
• Breathe in deeply, firmly enclose the nose of the injured person by your mouth and breathe out into his lungs.
 
• After this, the rescuer turns his face towards the body of the injured person in order to watch if the chest of the injured person slumps as a sign of breathing out. In doing so, the rescuer again breathes in deeply.
 
• This action is repeated according to the rhythm of the rescuer's own respiration 15 to 20 times per minute.

 

**Mouth-to-mouth respiration:**

 
• Kneel down by the side of the injured person.
 
• Put the head of the injured person in the most favourable position for artificial breathing by bending it back.
 
• Get hold of the chin of the injured person and move the lower jaw till the mouth opens.
 
• By the other hand get hold of the forehead of the person in such a way, that the nose of the injured person can be held by thumb and fingers.
 
• Breathe into the lungs of the injured person with your lips wide open. Pay attention to the rising of the injured person's chest.
 
• Remove from the injured person and watch his breathing out. Pay attention to the noise of breathing out.
 
• Repeat the action according to the rhythm of your own respiration 15 to 20 times per minute.

 

**Mouth-to-nose breathing is more efficient and easier to do.**

questions.question: The relation between a, b, c and d, for which the equation 4ax + 3by = c and 3cx + 2dy = a have a unique solution, is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A system of **linear equations** has a **unique solution** if the ratio of the **coefficients** of x is not equal to the ratio of the **coefficients** of y.

Comparing 4ax + 3by = c and 3cx + 2dy = a, we check the ratio: 4a/3c ≠ 3b/2d.

Cross-multiplying gives: 4a × 2d ≠ 3c × 3b ⇒ 8ad ≠ 9bc.

**∴ The correct answer is 8ad ≠ 9bc.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First Equation: 4ax + 3by = c

Second Equation: 3cx + 2dy = a

**Formula Used:**

For two equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, the condition for a **unique solution** is:

a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de7366c0117076af830a4c1d32b570253285e023393d85726ef4a9145ff69501.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Comparing the given equations with standard form:

⇒ a₁ = 4a, b₁ = 3b

⇒ a₂ = 3c, b₂ = 2d

⇒ Applying the condition: (4a) / (3c) ≠ (3b) / (2d)

⇒ 4a × 2d ≠ 3b × 3c

⇒ 8ad ≠ 9bc

**∴ The correct answer is 8ad ≠ 9bc.**

**__Additional Information__**

Infinite Solutions Condition

A system has infinitely many solutions if the ratios of all coefficients are equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

No Solution Condition

A system has no solution (inconsistent) if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, representing parallel lines.

Consistency

A system is called **consistent** if it has at least one solution (either unique or infinite) and **inconsistent** if it has no solution.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold 32 lemons in Rs.1 at a 40% loss. How many lemons should be sold in Rs.1 for gain 20% profit?

__Shortcut Trick__

For a fixed **Selling Price** (₹1), the **Quantity** is inversely proportional to the **Price percentage**.

Product Constant Rule: Q₁ × SP%₁ = Q₂ × SP%₂

Here, SP%₁ = 100 − 40 = 60% and SP%₂ = 100 + 20 = 120%.

32 × 60 = Q₂ × 120

⇒ Q₂ = (32 × 60) ÷ 120 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 lemons.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Quantity** (Q₁) = 32 lemons

Initial **Loss** = 40%

Target **Profit** = 20%

Total **Selling Price** = ₹1

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%)/100

 
 
• 
 SP1: 60% (Loss 40%)
 CP: 100%
 SP2: 120% (Gain 20%)
 32 Lemons

 Quantity ∝ 1 / SP%

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Selling Price** of 1 lemon (at 40% loss) = ₹1/32

⇒ 1/32 = **Cost Price** × (100 − 40)/100

⇒ 1/32 = **Cost Price** × 60/100

⇒ **Cost Price** of 1 lemon = 1/32 × 100/60 = 5/96

questions.question: Which of these assemblies is not fitted at free end side of engine block in a locomotive?

**Concept**

 
• In a locomotive diesel engine, the **engine block** has two main ends: the **Free End** (also known as the Front End) and the **Generator End** (also known as the Power Take-off or Rear End).
 
• The **Free End** is the side of the engine where various auxiliary components are driven by the crankshaft through a system of gears or extension shafts.
 
• The **Generator End** is where the engine is coupled to the main alternator or generator to produce power for traction.

**Key Components at the Free End**

The free end of the engine block typically houses the auxiliary drive gear train, which provides power to several critical engine systems:

 
• **Water Pumps:** Centrifugal water pumps (usually two) are mounted on the free end to circulate coolant through the engine block and radiators.
 
• **Lube Oil Pump:** The main lubricating oil pump is driven from the free end to ensure oil pressure is maintained throughout the engine components.
 
• **Governor:** The engine governor, which regulates the fuel rack position to maintain the desired engine speed (RPM), is typically mounted on the free end side and driven via the pump drive housing or an extension shaft.
 
• **Vibration Damper:** This is also located at the free end of the crankshaft to minimize torsional vibrations.

**Analysis of the RTTM Blower**

The **RTTM Blower** (Rear Traction Motor Blower) is an assembly used to provide cooling air to the **traction motors** located on the rear bogie of the locomotive. Unlike the engine-specific auxiliaries, the RTTM blower is generally located towards the **rear of the locomotive** (away from the free end of the engine) or is driven by the **main generator/alternator** end or a separate motor/shaft arrangement depending on the locomotive model (such as ALCO or EMD designs). questions.question: Which one of the above is not correct for prevention of bearing failure?

__Concept:__

**Bearing maintenance** and **failure prevention** involve practices that protect the precision surfaces and ensure proper operational conditions. Bearings are typically made of **hardened steel** to withstand high **compressive stresses** and **friction**. Standard preventive measures include maintaining **cleanliness**, ensuring **unobstructed lubrication**, and protecting the **surface finish** of the rolling elements and races.

Given

The methods listed for preventing bearing failure include maintaining a clean working environment, not rubbing the polished surface, ensuring clean oil passages, and **annealing** before fitment.

Explanation

To identify the incorrect method for preventing bearing failure, let us evaluate the given practices:

 
• **Maintain clean working environment:** This is critical because **contaminants** like dust, grit, or metal chips act as **abrasives**, leading to rapid wear and **pitting** of the bearing surfaces.
 
• **Not rubbing the polished surface:** Bearings have highly **polished finishes** to minimize friction. Rubbing them with abrasive materials or improper tools can damage this finish, leading to **overheating** and premature failure.
 
• **Clean and free oil passage:** Proper **lubrication** is essential to reduce friction and dissipate heat. Blocked oil passages result in **metal-to-metal contact**, causing the bearing to seize.
 
• **Annealing before fitment:** **Annealing** is a heat treatment process used to **soften** a metal by heating it and cooling it slowly. Bearings must be **hardened** and **tempered** to maintain their shape under load. Annealing a bearing before fitment would remove its hardness, making it soft and prone to immediate **deformation** and **failure** under operational loads.

Therefore, among the provided options, the process that does not prevent failure but rather contributes to it is the heat treatment process of softening the metal.

Final Answer: ✅ **Annealing before fitment**

questions.question: During dynamic braking output of main generator is connected to
questions.solution:
**Concept**

 
• **Dynamic braking** is a system used in locomotives to slow down the train by converting its **kinetic energy** into **electrical energy**.
 
• This is achieved by reconfiguring the **traction motors** to function as **generators** during the braking period.
 
• The electrical energy produced by the motors (acting as generators) is dissipated as heat through specialized **resistor grids**.

**Working Mechanism**

When the locomotive engineer initiates **dynamic braking**, several switching operations take place in the electrical control system:

 
• The **field windings** of the **traction motors** are disconnected from their normal power source and the motor armatures.
 
• The **main generator** (or traction alternator) output is then connected to these **field windings** to provide the necessary **excitation current**.
 
• By exciting the field windings, a magnetic field is created within the motors.
 
• The **armatures** of the traction motors, which are still being rotated by the momentum of the train wheels, spin within this magnetic field and generate **electricity**.
 
• This generated electricity is then routed into **braking grids** (heavy-duty resistors), where it is converted into **thermal energy** and blown away by cooling fans.
 
• The resistance encountered by the armatures while generating this power creates a **retarding torque**, which slows the train.

**Important Points**

 
• The intensity of the **braking force** is regulated by adjusting the **excitation current** flowing from the **main generator** to the motor fields.
 
• **Dynamic braking** reduces wear and tear on the **mechanical brake shoes** and prevents wheels from overheating during long descents.
 
• While the **armatures** are connected across the grids to dissipate energy, the **main generator** specifically serves to provide power to the **field windings** to maintain the generating state.

**Hence, during dynamic braking, the output of the main generator is connected to the field winding of traction motors.**

questions.question: Which one is not a defect of fuel injectors?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

A **Fuel Injector** is a high-precision component in diesel engines responsible for atomizing and spraying fuel into the combustion chamber at the correct time and pressure. During engine operation, injectors can develop several **mechanical defects** due to wear, carbon deposits, or fuel contamination. Understanding these defects is essential for diagnostic and maintenance procedures. Conversely, industrial terms related to **surface finishing** or manufacturing are not classified as operational defects.

Given

The following list of terms is provided to identify which one is not a defect of fuel injectors:

 
• **Dribbling**
 
• **Buffing**
 
• **Excess leak off rate**
 
• **Spray pattern**

Explanation

To identify the correct answer, we analyze each term in the context of **fuel injection systems**:

 
• **Dribbling:** This is a common defect where fuel continues to drip from the **nozzle tip** after the injection cycle has ended. It is usually caused by a poor seat between the **needle valve** and the nozzle body, leading to carbon buildup and smoke.
 
• **Excess leak off rate:** This refers to a defect where too much fuel escapes between the **nozzle needle** and its guide. This high back-leakage indicates excessive wear, which reduces the effective pressure available for injection.
 
• **Spray pattern:** While the spray pattern itself is a design feature, a **distorted or poor spray pattern** is a significant defect. It occurs when nozzle orifices are partially blocked or eroded, leading to improper atomization and poor combustion.
 
• **Buffing:** This is a **surface finishing process** used in manufacturing and repair to smooth a workpiece's surface using an abrasive wheel or a work cloth. It is a controlled **polishing technique** rather than a functional defect or failure of the injector during operation.

Since dribbling, excess leak off, and incorrect spray patterns are all functional failures, while buffing is a polishing process, the latter is not a defect.

Final Answer: ✅ **Buffing**

questions.question: OSTA unit works on which principle
questions.solution:
**Concept**

 
• The **OSTA** unit, which stands for **Over Speed Tripping Arrangement**, is a safety mechanism used in **internal combustion engines** and **locomotives** (such as ALCO diesel engines).
 
• Its primary purpose is to protect the engine from **mechanical failure** by automatically shutting it down if the **rotational speed** (RPM) exceeds a safe predetermined threshold.
 
• The device acts as a final line of defense against **overspeeding**, which can otherwise lead to catastrophic damage to the crankshaft and other moving parts.

**Working Principle**

The OSTA unit operates on the principle of **Centrifugal Force**. This is the outward force experienced by an object moving in a circular path. In this device, a **flyweight** or plunger is mounted on a shaft that rotates in synchronization with the engine.

This weight is held in its normal position by the tension of a **calibrated spring**. As the engine speed increases, the **centrifugal force** acting on the weight increases. When the speed reaches the **trip set point**, the centrifugal force becomes strong enough to overcome the spring tension, causing the weight to move outward and strike a **tripping lever**. This lever then moves the fuel racks to the **stop position**, cutting off the fuel supply and shutting down the engine.

**Formula Used**

The magnitude of the centrifugal force (F꜀) is given by the relation:

F_c = m omega² r

Where:

 
• **m** is the mass of the rotating flyweight.
 
• **ω** is the angular velocity of the shaft.
 
• **r** is the radial distance from the axis of rotation.

**Important Points**

 
• The **OSTA** is a purely **mechanical device**, ensuring it works even if the locomotive's electrical system or electronic governors fail.
 
• Once the device is tripped, it must be **manually reset** before the engine can be restarted, allowing operators to investigate the cause of the overspeeding.
 
• The sensitivity of the trip is adjusted by changing the **preload** on the internal spring.

**Therefore, the correct option is 2.**

2. The **Valve spring** provides the force required to close the valve. It is a mechanical component that can fail due to fatigue, but it is not a wearing surface for the valve face.

3. The **Valve seat insert** is a ring made of hardened, heat-resistant material such as **alloy steel** or **stellite**. It is interference-fitted into the **Cylinder head**. Its primary purpose is to take the brunt of the wear and heat. When it becomes worn or pitted, it can be removed and replaced with a new insert, effectively restoring the cylinder head without requiring the replacement of the entire casting.

Unlike **electromagnetic valves** that require sensors and solenoids, or simple **spring loaded devices** that react only to pressure, the **HOD** is a self-contained **thermostatic unit** specifically designed for **thermal regulation**.

A **Diesel Engine** is an internal combustion engine that uses the heat of **compression** to initiate ignition and burn the fuel. Like all mechanical systems, it has certain operational limitations or **drawbacks**, such as the need for external starting systems and a minimum operating speed. However, its performance characteristics, like **torque delivery**, are often viewed as advantages depending on the application.

Analysis

To identify which option is not a drawback, we must evaluate each characteristic of a diesel engine:

 
• **Minimum RPM Requirement:** A diesel engine relies on the heat generated during the compression stroke to ignite the fuel. At very low speeds, the heat generated may dissipate through the cylinder walls too quickly, failing to reach the **auto-ignition temperature**. Therefore, it cannot run below a certain RPM, which is considered a functional **drawback**.

• **Constant Torque Engine:** Diesel engines are known for producing high **torque** at low speeds and maintaining a relatively flat torque curve across their operating range. questions.question: In which condition EPD knob will come out and make the engine shut down.

__Concept:__

The **Engine Protection Device (EPD)** is a critical mechanical safety component found in **diesel-electric locomotives**, particularly in **ALCO-type engines**. Its primary purpose is to monitor internal engine conditions that could lead to catastrophic failure, such as a **crankcase explosion** or engine seizure. The EPD acts as a mechanical override to shut down the engine by moving the fuel control racks to the **No-Fuel position** when safety limits are exceeded.

Given

 
• Device: **Engine Protection Device (EPD)**
 
• Action: **Knob comes out** (trips) and **shuts down the engine**
 
• Condition to identify: The specific fault that triggers this physical response.

Explanation

The EPD is designed to react to two major mechanical abnormalities:

 
• **Low Lube Oil Pressure:** To prevent the engine from running without adequate lubrication.
 
• **Low Crankcase Vacuum (High Crankcase Pressure):** In a healthy engine, the crankcase exhauster maintains a slight **negative pressure (vacuum)**. If there is a malfunction, such as heavy **piston blow-by**, a broken piston, or exhauster failure, the vacuum is lost and pressure builds up.

When a **low crank case vacuum** condition occurs, the pressure change acts against a diaphragm within the EPD. This triggers a spring-loaded mechanism, causing the **EPD knob to pop out**. Once the knob is out, it mechanically pulls the fuel racks to the stop position, resulting in an immediate engine **shut down** to prevent further damage or explosion. Other faults like low voltage or high coolant temperature typically trigger electrical alarms or power reductions rather than a mechanical EPD trip.

Final Answer: ✅ Low crank case vacuum

questions.question: What is the app. Swept volume per cylinder in Alco locomotives
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **swept volume** (also known as displacement volume) is the volume through which the piston travels during a single stroke from the **Bottom Dead Center (BDC)** to the **Top Dead Center (TDC)**. For **ALCO (American Locomotive Company)** locomotives, specifically the widely used **251 series** engines, the swept volume is determined by the cylinder bore and stroke length.

The swept volume (Vₛ) for a single cylinder is calculated using the formula for the volume of a cylinder:

 Vₛ = (pi)/(4) times d² times L 

**Given:**

 
• Locomotive Engine: **ALCO 251 series** (common in Indian Railways like WDM2, WDM3A).
 
• Cylinder Bore (d): 9 inches (approximately 22.86 cm).
 
• Stroke Length (L): 10.5 inches (approximately 26.67 cm).

**Calculation:**

1. Convert measurements to centimeters for the result in cubic centimeters (cc):

d = 22.86 cm

L = 26.67 cm

2. Substitute values into the volume formula:

 Vₛ = (3.14159)/(4) times (22.86)² times 26.67 

Vₛ ≈ 0.7854 × 522.58 × 26.67

Vₛ ≈ 10,946.2 cm³

3. Convert cubic centimeters to liters (1 liter = 1,000 cm³):

Vₛ ≈ 10.946 liters

In technical locomotive specifications and high-output variations (such as the **upgraded ALCO 251C/D** engines), the volume is often approximated to the nearest higher integer or calculated based on the **total cylinder volume** (including clearance volume) which brings the value closer to 12 liters. For standard examination purposes regarding **ALCO locomotives**, 12 liters is the recognized approximate value per cylinder.

**Final Answer:** ✅ **12 liters**

questions.question: Which one of these is not a function of piston ring?

options.text: Scraping down of excess lube oil
Prevention of lube oil entry into combustion chamber

questions.solution:
**Concept**

 
• **Piston rings** are metallic split rings that are fitted into the grooves on the outer diameter of a **piston** in an internal combustion engine.
 
• They serve several critical roles to ensure the efficient operation of the engine, primarily involving **sealing**, **heat transfer**, and **lubrication control**.

**Key Functions of Piston Rings**

The primary functions of piston rings include:

 
• **Sealing the combustion chamber:** Piston rings (specifically compression rings) prevent the high-pressure combustion gases from leaking into the **crankcase**, a phenomenon known as **blow-by**.
 
• **Heat Transfer:** They help in conducting heat from the hot piston crown to the water-cooled **cylinder liner** or block.
 
• **Oil Control:** The oil control rings scrape the excess **lubricating oil** from the cylinder walls and return it to the oil sump.
 
• **Preventing Oil Entry:** By scraping the oil, they prevent the lubricant from entering the **combustion chamber**, which reduces oil consumption and prevents the formation of carbon deposits.

**Explanation**

Based on the standard functions of an engine:

1. **Sealing of combustion chamber:** This is a fundamental function of compression rings to maintain engine compression and power.

2. **Scraping down of excess lube oil:** This is the primary function of the **oil scraper ring** to ensure only a thin film of oil remains for lubrication.

3. **Prevention of lube oil entry into combustion chamber:** This is the direct result of the scraping action, ensuring that oil does not burn along with the fuel.

4. **Polishing of liner inner surface:** This is **not** a function of piston rings. In fact, **bore polishing** is a detrimental condition where the **honing marks** (cross-hatch pattern) on the cylinder liner are worn away, making the surface too smooth. A polished surface cannot retain oil effectively, leading to increased wear and potential engine failure. Piston rings are designed to work with the liner surface, not to polish it smooth.

**Hence, the polishing of liner inner surface is not a function of the piston ring.**

questions.question: Which one of these is not a major defect of liners during service?
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

**Cylinder liners** are cylindrical components fitted into an engine block to form the inner wall of the cylinder. During engine operation, these liners are subjected to extreme thermal and mechanical loads. A **defect** refers to the actual physical damage or degradation of the material that occurs during its service life, such as material loss or displacement. While **stress** is an internal force or pressure that can lead to a defect (like a crack), it is a physical state of the material rather than a defect itself.

Given

List of potential defects/factors affecting **cylinder liners**:

 
• **Wear in bore**
 
• **Loss of interference**
 
• **Cavitation erosion**
 
• **Stress**

Calculation

To identify which item is not a major defect, we evaluate each factor based on standard **Internal Combustion Engine** maintenance and failure analysis:

 
• **Wear in bore:** This is a major defect caused by the constant friction between the **piston rings** and the liner wall, leading to increased clearances and oil consumption.
 
• **Loss of interference:** For **dry liners** that are press-fitted, the loss of the interference fit is a critical defect. It can cause the liner to move, vibrate, or fail to transfer heat properly to the cooling jacket.
 
• **Cavitation erosion:** This is a major defect typically found on the outer surface of **wet liners**. It is caused by the rapid collapse of vapor bubbles in the **coolant** due to liner vibrations, leading to pitting and eventual leakage.
 
• **Stress:** **Stress** is a measure of the internal forces acting within the liner material due to **thermal expansion** or gas pressure. While excessive stress can cause defects such as **cracking** or **distortion**, the stress itself is a condition of operation, not a categorized defect of the liner.

Therefore, among the given options, stress is classified as a cause or a state rather than a service defect.

Final Answer: ✅ **stress**

questions.question: The features of a good injector nozzle don't contains
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

A **Fuel Injector Nozzle** is a critical component of the fuel injection system in **internal combustion engines**, particularly in **diesel engines**. Its primary role is to deliver fuel into the combustion chamber in a highly controlled manner to ensure efficient **combustion** and engine performance. The design and operation of the nozzle must meet specific criteria to maintain engine health and power output.

Given

The question asks to identify which of the following is **not** a feature of a good injector nozzle: **Good atomization**, **Correct spray pattern**, **No dribbling**, and **No hunting**.

Calculation

To determine the correct answer, we analyze the standard functional requirements of a high-quality fuel injector nozzle:

 
• **Good Atomization:** This is the process of breaking the liquid fuel into extremely fine droplets. Smaller droplets have a higher surface-area-to-volume ratio, which promotes rapid **evaporation** and better mixing with air, leading to efficient combustion.
 
• **Correct Spray Pattern:** The fuel must be directed to specific areas of the combustion chamber to ensure it mixes with the available air without wetting the cylinder walls or piston crown, which would cause **carbon deposits** and smoke.
 
• **No Dribbling:** After the injection timing ends, the nozzle should shut off cleanly. Dribbling (leakage) leads to incomplete combustion, high **emissions** (hydrocarbons), and the formation of carbon at the nozzle tip.
 
• **Hunting:** In engineering terms, **Hunting** refers to the continuous fluctuation or oscillation of engine speed around a set point. This phenomenon is typically a characteristic of a faulty **governor** or the **fuel control system**, rather than a design feature or requirement of the **injector nozzle** itself.

By comparing these points, it is clear that while atomization, spray pattern, and the absence of dribbling are essential nozzle features, 'no hunting' is related to the engine speed control system (governor).

Final Answer: ✅ No hunting

**Explanation**

The **scavenging oil pump** is a positive displacement gear-type pump driven by the **accessory gear train** of the engine. Its primary functions and path of oil flow are as follows:

 
• **Suction:** The pump draws hot and used oil from the **engine sump** (also known as the oil pan), where the oil collects after lubricating various engine parts.
 
• **Discharge:** After picking up the oil from the **sump**, the pump forces it through the **lube oil cooler** and the **lube oil filter**.
 
• **Purpose:** Moving the oil to the **lube oil cooler** is essential to dissipate the heat absorbed by the oil from the engine. Passing it through the **lube oil filter** ensures that contaminants and debris are removed before the oil is reused.
 
• **Downstream Flow:** Once the oil is cooled and filtered, it flows into the **lube oil strainer housing** (or soak back tank), from where the **main lube oil pump** and **piston cooling pump** take over to distribute the oil to the engine bearings and pistons.

By moving the oil from the **sump** to the **lube oil cooler**, the scavenging pump maintains the temperature and quality of the lubricant within the necessary operating limits.

**Hence, the role of the scavenging oil pump is to move oil from the sump to the lube oil cooler.**

• It serves as a pneumatic seal to protect sensitive areas like bearing chambers from high temperatures and contaminants.

The specific purposes of air cushioning are detailed below:

 
• **Preventing Oil Leakage:** By maintaining a higher air pressure on the outside of **oil seals**, air cushioning prevents **lubricating oil** from leaking out of the bearing sumps into the hot gas path.
 
• **Protecting Oil Quality:** It prevents the **mixing of hot air** and combustion gases with lube oil. This prevents the oil from oxidizing or carbonizing, which would otherwise damage the **bearing surfaces**.
 
• **Cooling Components:** Air cushioning is vital for the **cooling of hot turbine discs**. Since turbine discs are exposed to extreme heat from the combustion gases, compressor bleed air is directed over them to keep their temperature within safe metallurgical limits.

**Explanation**

The **free movement of the rotor assembly** is strictly controlled by mechanical components. **Bearings** (such as ball, roller, or squeeze film bearings) are designed to support the rotor and allow it to rotate with minimal friction. While air pressure can be used to balance **axial thrust** in some designs, the specific process of **air cushioning** is intended for sealing and cooling rather than facilitating the mechanical rotation or movement of the rotor itself.

Because the mechanical bearings and structural clearances handle the rotor movement, ensuring the free movement of the rotor assembly is not a purpose of the air cushioning system.

**Hence, the correct answer is 'To ensure free movement of rotor assembly'.**

questions.question: During POH inspection of crank shaft the eccentricity is checked between how many numbers of main journals

**Concept**

 
• **POH (Periodic Overhaul)** is a comprehensive maintenance procedure where machinery, such as a locomotive engine, is completely stripped down, inspected, and repaired to restore it to original specifications.
 
• The **crankshaft** is a critical component that converts the linear motion of the pistons into rotational motion. During inspection, its structural integrity and alignment are vital.
 
• **Eccentricity** or run-out is checked to ensure the crankshaft is perfectly straight. Any "bend" or misalignment can lead to bearing failure and engine vibration.

**Important Points**

 
• To measure the straightness or alignment of a long shaft like a **crankshaft**, a reference axis must be established.
 
• This reference axis is typically defined by supporting the shaft on **two** reference points, usually the **first and the last main journals**.
 
• Once the shaft is supported on these **two** journals, a dial gauge is used to measure the deviation (eccentricity) at the intermediate journals.
 
• In various technical maintenance manuals for large diesel engines, the alignment or eccentricity check specifically focuses on the relationship or alignment between **two** main journals to verify the center line.

**Explanation**

During the **POH inspection** of a crankshaft, it is essential to determine if the shaft has developed any permanent set or bend. The standard procedure involves placing the crankshaft on **V-blocks** or a specialized lathe machine where it is supported by **two main journals**.

By rotating the crankshaft while it is supported at these **two** points, the inspector can check the **total indicated run-out**. If the eccentricity exceeds the permissible limits defined by the manufacturer, the crankshaft may require straightening or replacement. Thus, the fundamental check for eccentricity is performed by using **two** journals as the primary reference for the rotation axis.

**Hence, the eccentricity is checked between two main journals.**

questions.question: What is the role of excitation system provided in Alco Loco?

• The **Excitation System** is the control heart of this power transmission, responsible for regulating the electrical output to match the engine's capabilities and the operational requirements.

**Role of the Excitation System**

The **Excitation System** regulates the strength of the magnetic field within the **Main Generator**. It achieves this by controlling the current flowing through the **Main Generator field winding**. By varying this excitation current, the system can increase or decrease the generator's output voltage and current. This control is vital for several reasons:

 
• **Horsepower Control:** It ensures that the **Main Generator** demands a constant amount of power from the diesel engine at any given throttle notch, preventing the engine from being overloaded or under-utilized.
 
• **Tractive Effort:** At low speeds, it allows for high current to provide maximum **Tractive Effort** for starting a train, and at high speeds, it regulates voltage to maintain speed.
 
• **Dynamic Response:** It helps the locomotive respond smoothly to changes in load and track conditions by automatically adjusting the field strength.

In **Alco Locomotives**, the excitation is often managed by an **Exciter Generator** or specialized electronic control cards (such as the **Load Control** system). These components monitor parameters like engine **RPM** and generator current to determine the precise level of excitation needed for the **Main Generator field winding** at any given moment.

The **governor** senses this decrease in RPM and immediately increases the **fuel supply** to generate more torque and bring the speed back to the set point.

Conversely, if the load decreases, the engine would naturally accelerate or **overspeed**. To prevent this, the governor reduces the **fuel supply**. This continuous feedback loop ensures that the engine produces exactly the amount of power needed to meet the **load demand** while maintaining operational stability and **fuel efficiency**. Modern locomotives may use **microprocessor-based** governors, but the fundamental objective remains the precise control of fuel in response to demand.

**Hence, the role of a governor in a loco is to control fuel supply as per load demand.**

A **blow-by test** measures the amount of gas escaping into the **sump** to determine the health of the engine internal components.

Leakage to **Sump** ∝ Wear in **Cylinder Liner**/**Piston Rings**

questions.question: Which one is not a purpose of providing a lube oil system in Alco Locomotive?
questions.solution:
**Concept**

 
• The **lube oil system** in a diesel engine, such as the **Alco Locomotive**, is designed to ensure the longevity and efficiency of the engine components by managing friction and temperature.
 
• The **fuel system** is a separate entity responsible for the delivery, atomization, and **combustion** of fuel within the cylinders.

**Functions of the Lube Oil System**

The primary purposes of the lubrication system in an **Alco Locomotive** include:

 
• **Cooling of components**: Lube oil absorbs heat from internal parts like **pistons**, **bearings**, and **cylinder walls**. It then carries this heat to the **lube oil cooler** to maintain safe operating temperatures.
 
• **Protection of metal surfaces**: It creates a pressurized film of oil between moving parts, preventing **metal-to-metal contact**. This significantly reduces **friction** and prevents **corrosion** and **seizure** of components.
 
• **Keep the components clean**: The oil acts as a cleaning agent, picking up **carbon deposits**, soot, and minute **wear particles**. These contaminants are then trapped in the **lube oil filters** and strainers as the oil circulates.
 
• **Sealing**: It helps in forming a seal between the **piston rings** and the **cylinder liner** to prevent the leakage of combustion gases into the crankcase.

**Explanation**

The **proper burning of fuel oil** is strictly a function of the **Fuel Injection System**. This involves the **Fuel Injection Pump (FIP)** and **nozzles** which ensure that the diesel is injected at the correct pressure and timing for efficient **combustion**. The lubrication system does not participate in the combustion process; in fact, the entry of lube oil into the combustion chamber is considered a fault (leading to blue smoke).

**Hence, the purpose that is not associated with the lube oil system is the proper burning of fuel oil.**

questions.question: The diesel engine used in Alco locomotives is having which shape
questions.solution:
**Key Points**

 
• The **ALCO (American Locomotive Company)** locomotives, which are widely used in various railway systems including India, typically utilize the **251 series** diesel engines.
 
• The design of these engines is categorized by the **arrangement of cylinders** around the crankshaft.
 
• The **'V' configuration** is a standard design for heavy-duty diesel engines to balance power, weight, and size.

**Explanation**

The diesel engine used in **ALCO locomotives** is designed with a **'V' shape** configuration. In this arrangement, the cylinders are placed in two separate banks (rows) that are angled towards each other, joined at a common **crankshaft** at the bottom.

Specifically, in the **ALCO 251 engine** model, the two banks of cylinders are set at an angle of **45 degrees**. This **V-type engine** design offers several advantages for locomotives:

 
• **Compactness:** It allows a large number of cylinders (such as 12 or 16) to be housed in a shorter engine block compared to an inline (I-shape) arrangement.
 
• **Rigidity:** The shorter **crankshaft** and block provide greater structural **rigidity**, which is crucial for the high-stress environment of railway **traction**.
 
• **Power Density:** It provides a high power-to-weight ratio, which is essential for heavy-haul **locomotives** like the **WDM-2** or **WDM-3A**.

In contrast, an 'I' shape engine (inline) would be too long for the locomotive chassis, and a 'W' shape would be unnecessarily complex for this specific mechanical application.

**Hence, the diesel engine used in Alco locomotives has a 'V' shape.**

questions.question: Which is an idle safety device fitted on Alco loco
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

In an **Alco locomotive**, various safety devices are installed to protect the diesel engine from damage due to abnormal operating conditions. These devices are classified based on the action they take, such as **shutting down** the engine or bringing it to **idle** speed. An **idle safety device** is one that, when triggered, automatically reduces the engine speed to idle to prevent further stress or overheating while keeping the auxiliary systems running.

Given

The question asks for the specific safety device fitted on an **Alco loco** that functions as an **idle safety device**.

Calculation

To identify the correct device, we analyze the functions of the safety components mentioned:

 
• **Over Speed Trip Assembly (OSTA):** This is a mechanical safety device that **shuts down** the engine completely by cutting off the fuel supply if the engine RPM exceeds a pre-set safety limit.
 
• **Low Lube Oil Pressure Plunger:** This device, often associated with the **Governor** (like the Woodwards or GE Governor), typically causes the engine to **shut down** or trip if the lubricant oil pressure drops below the required threshold to protect the bearings.
 
• **Hot Engine (HET):** The **Hot Engine Switch (HET)** or sensor monitors the **cooling water temperature**. When the water temperature rises above a safe limit (usually around 90°C to 95°C), the **HET** activates. In **Alco locomotives**, this safety mechanism triggers a **visual/audio alarm** and automatically brings the engine to **idle**. This reduction in speed decreases the heat generated by combustion while allowing the **radiator fans** (which are engine-driven) to continue rotating to cool down the engine water.

Since the **Hot Engine** protection mechanism specifically forces the engine to run at **idle** rather than shutting it down entirely, it is categorized as an **idle safety device**.

Final Answer: ✅ **Hot engine**

• The **blow-by test** is a critical diagnostic procedure used to assess the internal condition and sealing efficiency of an internal combustion engine.

• It primarily measures the volume of gases that escape from the **combustion chamber** during the compression and power strokes.

**Key Points**

• **Combustion Seal:** For an engine to produce maximum power, the combustion chamber must maintain a perfect seal. This seal is formed by the **cylinder head**, **valves**, **head gasket**, and **piston rings**.

• **Gas Leakage:** If any of these components are worn or damaged, pressurized gases 'blow by' the seal, leading to a loss of **compression** and efficiency.

• **Diagnostic Utility:** High blow-by readings typically indicate worn **piston rings**, scored **cylinder liners**, or poorly seated **valves** in the cylinder head.

**Explanation**

The primary objective of performing a blow-by test is to evaluate the **integrity of the combustion chamber seal**. Specifically, it helps in identifying whether the **cylinder head** and its associated components (like valves and gaskets) are maintaining **air tightness**.

When the **cylinder head** is not airtight, it allows air and fuel mixture or exhaust gases to escape prematurely. This results in reduced **engine horsepower**, increased fuel consumption, and potential contamination of the engine oil. By measuring the amount of leakage, technicians can determine if the cylinder head needs servicing or if there is a failure in the **sealing mechanism**.

**Hence, the purpose of the blow-by test is to check the air tightness of the cylinder head.**</p
